sn5.4:0.3: The Discourse about Vijayā Thus I have heard:
sn5.4:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.4:1.2: Then the nun Vijayā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms. After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day, and having entered Blind Man’s Wood,
sn5.4:1.3: she sat down at the root of a certain tree to pass the day.
sn5.4:1.4: Then the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in the nun Vijayā, desiring to drive her out of concentration, approached the nun Vijayā, and after approaching he addressed the nun Vijayā with a verse:
sn5.4:2.2: and I am a youthful man,
sn5.4:2.3: Come, Sister, let us enjoy ourselves with the fivefold musical instruments.”
sn5.4:3.1: Then it occurred to the nun Vijayā:
sn5.4:3.2: “Who is this, a human or a non-human, speaking this verse?”
sn5.4:3.3: Then it occurred to the nun Vijayā:
sn5.4:3.4: “This is the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in me, desiring to drive me out of concentration, who speaks this verse.”
sn5.4:3.5: Then the nun Vijayā having understood: This is the Wicked Māra, replied with these verses to the Wicked Māra:
sn5.4:4.1: “Delightful forms, sounds, tastes, smells and touches,
sn5.4:4.3: I assign (them) to you, Māra, I am not seeking for that.
sn5.4:5.4: and have rooted up sensual craving.
sn5.4:6.1: There are beings who reached form,
sn5.4:6.2: and those in the formless state,
sn5.4:6.3: (But) those who have attained to peace have destroyed darkness everywhere.”
sn5.4:7.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Vijayā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
